description:
Trigger: caller invokes `new_with_signer_discovery` with a bundle in which the discovered signer carries an AKI keyIdentifier but the bundle is missing the cert whose SKI matches; the bundle DOES contain a same-DN different-key cert (the key-rollover bridge scenario in reverse).

discover_crl_signer (pkix-revocation/src/signer_discovery.rs:100-105) explicitly returns None on AKI-present-but-no-SKI-match, with rationale: 'A bundle that has the right DN but the wrong key would otherwise hijack discovery — exactly the case AKI is designed to prevent.'

find_parent (pkix-revocation/src/signer_discovery.rs:186-205) does the OPPOSITE on the same input shape: it loops over bundle looking for AKI/SKI match, and on no-match silently continues to the issuer-DN fallback (line 201-204). This means reaches_self_signed can succeed by walking through same-DN-different-key bridges that AKI was supposed to prevent.

Bad behavior: structural anchor-reachability check accepts a chain that AKI semantics say should be rejected. Today this is mitigated by the doc-level 'no signature verification; bundle pre-validation is caller's responsibility' stance — but the inconsistency is a footgun: discover_crl_signer's behavior and find_parent's behavior disagree on the same primitive.

Fix options:
1. Mirror discover_crl_signer's strict semantics in find_parent: AKI present and no SKI match → return None (no DN fallback). Aligns the two functions on the same anti-hijack rule.
2. Mirror find_parent's lenient semantics in discover_crl_signer: drop the early return. Loses the §4.5 PKITS discriminator property; not viable.

(1) is the correct fix. Add a unit test that constructs a bundle with [bridge_with_AKI, same_DN_cert_no_matching_SKI] and asserts reaches_self_signed returns false.
title: find_parent silently falls through AKI→DN; discover_crl_signer does not
